mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly ranks the magnitude of repulsion between electron pairs around a central atom according to VSEPR theory?

options.A: Bonding pair–bonding pair > lone pair–bonding pair > lone pair–lone pair
options.B: Lone pair–lone pair > bonding pair–bonding pair > lone pair–bonding pair
options.C: Lone pair–lone pair > lone pair–bonding pair > bonding pair–bonding pair
options.D: Bonding pair–bonding pair > lone pair–lone pair > lone pair–bonding pair

mcqs.answer: Lone pair–lone pair > lone pair–bonding pair > bonding pair–bonding pair
mcqs.explanation: VSEPR theory states that repulsion strength follows: lone‑pair–lone‑pair (strongest) > lone‑pair–bonding‑pair > bonding‑pair–bonding‑pair (weakest). Option C reflects this order, while the other options place the repulsions in an incorrect sequence.

mcqs.question: A molecule has a central atom surrounded by four electron pairs, of which two are bonding pairs and two are lone pairs. What is the molecular geometry of this molecule?
mcqs.explanation: Four electron pairs give a tetrahedral electron‑pair geometry. When two of those are lone pairs, they occupy equatorial positions and push the two bonding pairs together, producing a bent (V‑shaped) molecular geometry. The other options correspond to different steric numbers or lone‑pair arrangements.

mcqs.question: Molecule (i) CH₄ has four bonding pairs and no lone pairs around carbon. Molecule (ii) SF₄ has four bonding pairs and one lone pair around sulfur. Which statement correctly describes the effect of the lone pair on the bond angles between the bonding pairs?

options.A: SF₄ has a larger bond angle than CH₄ because lone pairs increase repulsion.
options.B: SF₄ has a smaller bond angle than CH₄ because lone pairs compress the bonding pairs.
options.C: Both molecules have the same bond angle because only bonding pairs determine geometry.
options.D: SF₄ is linear while CH₄ is bent, so their bond angles cannot be compared.

mcqs.answer: SF₄ has a smaller bond angle than CH₄ because lone pairs compress the bonding pairs.
mcqs.explanation: A lone pair occupies more space than a bonding pair, exerting greater repulsion on adjacent bonding pairs. In SF₄ the lone‑pair–bonding‑pair repulsion reduces the X‑S‑X angles below the ideal tetrahedral angle (≈109.5°) observed in CH₄, which has only bonding pairs. Hence SF₄ shows smaller bond angles. Options A, C, and D misinterpret the role of lone pairs or the actual geometries.

mcqs.question: According to VSEPR theory, what is the approximate bond angle between the three bonding pairs in a trigonal pyramidal molecule such as NH₃?
mcqs.explanation: A trigonal pyramidal molecule has a tetrahedral electron‑pair arrangement (ideal angle 109.5°). The presence of a lone pair on the central atom exerts greater repulsion, compressing the H‑N‑H bond angles to about 107°. Option B matches this observed value; the other angles correspond to different geometries (square planar, ideal tetrahedral, trigonal planar).
